commit_subject: Kingston #46 closeout: encoder pin + re-emitted module + waiver removal (atomic) (#158)
description: drop the ungrounded annual_taper_denominator (5); derive withdrawal_rate = daily_taper_rate * days_per_week (2 6/7 per cent x 7 = 20 per cent, manual pages 28/40)

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module computed the class E taper as 1 divided by an invented parameter `annual_taper_denominator = 5` whose proof atom cited page-28 text ('amount B is 2 6/7 per cent') that states no denominator of 5 and no annualization, so the taper rate rested on a value with no basis in the cited provision instead of on the source's daily 2 6/7 per cent rate converted over seven days.
triage.triage_notes: Single module in the commit; the module diff is only two hunks (39 lines). Hunk 1 deletes the entire `annual_taper_denominator` parameter rule (value 5, source line 'annualized class E amount B percentage', proof excerpt 'amount B is 2 6/7 per cent' at page-28) and extends the `daily_taper_rate` literal from 0.02857142857142857 to 0.02857142857142857142857142857; hunk 2 rewrites `withdrawal_rate` from `1 / ..._annual_taper_denominator` to `..._daily_taper_rate * ..._days_per_week`. Provision WAS read through the pinned release: page-28 says '(ii) amount B is 2 6/7 per cent of the difference between his income for the relevant week and his applicable amount' within class E ('On any day class E consists of...'), and contains no 5 and no annualization — confirming the deleted parameter was ungrounded. Important caveat for a reviewer: the numeric outcome is unchanged (1/5 = 0.2 and the 28-digit daily literal x 7 = exactly 0.2, which is why all 7 companion tests hold unchanged), so this is a grounding/derivation defect rather than a value defect; if the corpus wants only behavior-changing defects this one is a boundary case, but the maintainers tracked it as a real defect (issue #46 with an active validation waiver) and the PR body calls the deleted parameter 'fabricated'. The module header (singular source_verification with the page-38 locator) is byte-identical to the parent because PR commits 2 and 3 undid the re-emitter's plural corpus_citation_paths/upstream_source_check shape, so none of that contract churn appears in the net diff. Other files in the commit (.axiom/toolchain.toml, both workflow YAMLs, known-validation-gaps.yaml, the release fingerprint JSON) are pin/waiver bookkeeping, not rule content. Corroborating quotes: PR body — 'fabricated `annual_taper_denominator=5` deleted'; PR issue comment (Sol verdict) — 'the withdrawal rate is transparently derived as daily rate x 7 rather than through the erroneous denominator.'
triage.verifier_justification: The pre-fix module carried a source-attributed parameter rule (`kind: parameter`, `source: "... annualized class E amount B percentage"`) whose value was `5` and whose only proof atom cited page-28 with the excerpt "amount B is 2 6/7 per cent"; I resolved page-28 through the pinned release (uk-rulespec-2026-07-14, corpus 592ac643) and its class E text states only "amount B is 2 6/7 per cent of the difference between his income for the relevant week and his applicable amount" — no denominator of 5, no annualization, no 20 per cent — so the module's class E taper rested on a value the cited provision does not state, and the fix deletes that parameter and re-grounds `withdrawal_rate` on the source's own daily rate times the manual's daily conversion (page-40: "£17.31 x 1/7"). That is exactly "a value with no basis in the cited source (the fix removes or re-grounds it)". I tried the two available refutations and both fail: mechanical is excluded because a parameter rule is deleted and a formula rewritten (parameters/formulas did not stay the same), and amount_mismatch fits worse because the taper is 20 per cent before and after — the 17→28 digit extension of `daily_taper_rate` is a representation device so the engine product is exactly 0.2, not a correction of a wrong rate. The only real weakness is that no computed output changes (companions stay 7/7), but the taxonomy's untraceable_branch is precisely the grounding-level kind, and the repo treated it as a live validation gap (waiver #46, removed by this same commit).

triage.verifier_notes: Diff is 2 insertions / 19 deletions in the module, all inside the taper chain. Pre-fix: `daily_taper_rate` (0.02857142857142857) and `days_per_week` (7) existed but were dead — nothing referenced them; `withdrawal_rate = 1 / annual_taper_denominator` = 0.2. Post-fix: the denominator rule is gone, `withdrawal_rate = daily_taper_rate * days_per_week`, and the daily literal is widened to 28 digits (0.02857142857142857142857142857, a truncation of 1/35 = 2 6/7%) so the engine product is exactly 0.2. The single consumer (line 484/501, `excess_income_for_year * withdrawal_rate`) is untouched, so behavior is numerically unchanged — a reviewer who requires an output-visible delta for "fidelity" could push this to unclear/mechanical, but "mechanical" as defined here is unavailable because a parameter rule and a formula changed. Source verification: page-28 (class E, para 17(f)(ii)) grounds 2 6/7 per cent of the weekly excess and nothing else; page-40 (para 30A) grounds the manual's weekly→daily "x 1/7" convention behind days_per_week = 7. Commit message and PR body corroborate ("drop the ungrounded annual_taper_denominator (5)"; "fabricated `annual_taper_denominator=5` deleted"). Note the commit is a 4-part stack that also touches waivers, toolchain pins and the release manifest, but those live in other_files; the module file itself changed only as described. Also note the module header locator moved to page-38 in this commit (module-level metadata, not part of the defect).
